question: The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons of which religion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons **Buddhist**.
 
• The Pāla Empire emerged as a dominant force in the Indian subcontinent during the post-classical period, with its roots in the Bengal region.
 
• Named after its ruling dynasty, characterized by rulers bearing names ending with the suffix Pāla, which signifies "protector" in Prakrit, the empire's foundation can be traced back to the late eighth century CE, with the ascension of Gopāla as the emperor of Gauda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Pāla Empire** exerted its influence primarily in Bengal and eastern Bihar, encompassing key cities such as Gauḍa, Vikramapura, Pāṭaliputra, Monghyr, Somapura, Ramavati (Varendra), Tāmralipta, and Jaggadala.
 
• This period is regarded as one of the golden eras in Bengali history, marked by stability and prosperity brought forth by the Palas after centuries of internal strife and civil war among rival factions.
 
• Under Pāla rule, there was significant advancement in various aspects of Bengali civilization, with notable contributions to arts and architecture.
 
• The Palas not only built upon the achievements of preceding Bengali civilizations but also produced remarkable works of art and architectural marvels, further enriching the cultural heritage of the region.
